# task-cf69f9ec: closed rectangular frame fill

## When to Use
Use on task-cf69f9ec instances with color-5 rectangular scaffolds on color-9 background.

For task id `task-cf69f9ec`, inspect the color-5 scaffold on background 9. Fill the strict interior of fully closed rectangular frames with color 4; preserve every color-5 border and all other cells, including open/incomplete frame-like structures.

## Evidence from a solved instance

Input was 15x22, background 9 and frame color 5. Three closed rectangles were present:
- rows 3–7, columns 8–14: strict interior rows 4–6, columns 9–13 turned to 4 (3x5).
- rows 3–7, columns 14–21: strict interior rows 4–6, columns 15–20 turned to 4 (3x6). Shared border at column 14 remains color 5.
- rows 9–14, columns 8–12: strict interior rows 10–13, columns 9–11 turned to 4 (4x3).
All other scaffold cells and background stayed unchanged. First two frames share a vertical wall; treat each as a separate closed enclosure.

## Important distinction
A scaffold that looks almost rectangular but has an absent side/open perimeter must not be filled. In this instance, rows 9–12, columns 8–12 had top and partial vertical sides but was not closed; it remained entirely color 5/9. Isolated or dangling color-5 lines are untouched.

## Procedure
1. Identify axis-aligned color-5 rectangular perimeters with all four sides continuously present.
2. For each closed rectangle, recolor only strict interior cells (excluding perimeter) to 4.
3. Leave open frames, other color-5 marks, and all 9s outside interiors unchanged.
4. Check shared walls carefully: they remain 5, while each adjacent closed rectangle's strict interior is filled independently.
5. Return the complete grid preserving dimensions and all unchanged cells.
